SUBSTRATE ACCUMULATION MODEL

SAM Volume I
Substrate and Accumulation
Chapters I–XII

Sean Brady
Originator and conceptual director

Unified expanded working edition
19 October 2026

This edition brings the twelve chapters into one continuous manuscript. Chapters I–V retain the submitted mathematical text;
Chapter VI is retypeset from its integrated source without its separate contents pages. Chapters VII–XII are substantially expanded
with worked derivations, explicit physical assumptions, and reproducible arithmetic checks. A reconciled evidence appendix
replaces the earlier closing review and interface list. Chapters I–VI were developed with OpenAI ChatGPT and Codex, with the contributor
credits recorded in the individual chapters retained. The submitted Chapter VII and initial VIII–XII drafts, and the earlier closing review, credit
Claude/Claude Code under Sean Brady’s direction. The present expansion, source recovery, editorial reconciliation and unified assembly were
prepared with OpenAI ChatGPT and Codex. These credits describe the development history, not independent scientific endorsement.

How to read this edition
A physical construction with its assumptions visible
The volume moves from finite source histories and retained accounts to spatial response, clocks and signals, strong fields, quantum records,
boundary thermodynamics, cosmic inventory, thermal history, halos, radiation and possible cosmic futures. The same word can describe different
mathematical objects in these settings. A count is not automatically a mass; a propagation account is not automatically a density; a finite source
calculation is not automatically a long-time cosmological law. Each join must identify the receiving law, its units, and the observable it supplies.
The expanded chapters separate exact identities, theorems under declared assumptions, results reported by retained computational records, and
physical hypotheses awaiting selection or calibration. The new worked examples are analytic comparisons and finite arithmetic checks. They do
not constitute new native GEN6 campaigns, new observational fits, or experimental validation. Where the submitted closing review claimed more
than its evidence established, Appendix A records the narrower conclusion and the remaining interface.

Continuity with the submitted manuscript
The latest submitted content, rather than an older shorter chapter, is the preservation baseline. Chapters I–III match their earlier formatting sources exactly. The integrated source for Chapter IV, Chapter V and Chapter VI was recovered from the archived research revision
6890eae4cb5f33c766c86ce10f43b5165a4c4157. The original vector content of Chapters I–V is retained, with harmonized running
headers and continuous folios. Chapter VI retains its complete source-derived body and proofs while changing its layout. Historical dates, receipt
identifiers and claims of historical verification keep their original scope.
Some retained passages describe earlier development stages. Read them together with their later continuation and the current evidence appendix.
A historical section’s list of open tasks is not necessarily the final status of the chapter. Conversely, a conditional closure is not promoted to an
unconditional physical law by inclusion in this volume. References to old packet pages identify those archived packets unless an explicit chapter
and current volume page is given.

Sources, code and verification
The companion source package contains the editable chapter sources, figures, manuscript build instructions, source-recovery provenance, new
arithmetic checks and assembly verification. The evidence appendix inventories the earlier review’s identifiers so that revised conclusions remain
traceable. Historical native evidence and observational results are reported from their sources; they have not been represented as rerun for this
edition.
The opening chapter’s public data repository is https://github.com/iwtbotiwtwot/sam_volume_I_i; Chapter II’s is
https://github.com/iwtbotiwtwot/sam_volume_I_ii. Other chapter-specific source records and references remain with their
respective chapters. The archived research revision used for source recovery is identified in the companion provenance manifest. Repository
accessibility and the presence of a receipt do not replace checking its mathematical or empirical scope.

What the expansion is intended to accomplish
The later chapters now explain the intermediate calculations that short drafts left implicit: thermodynamic balances and accessible information; the
dimensionful inventory cascade; recombination and visibility; potential, force and halo inversion; radiative flux and spectral boundary conditions;
and conservation, causal horizons and future evolution. Solved examples expose which conclusions follow from the stated equations and which
require an additional physical law. This is a fuller working manuscript for scientific review, with no imposed chapter page limit.

Abstract. Original signed Write histories supply phase and action data that can be received into a finite pair source coupled to a
two-polarization quadrupole field. This chapter keeps the original rules, the receiving laws, and their derived consequences
explicit. A four-component source yields six driven spectral lanes and four unforced states. For a declared coherent hard-field
preparation in each lane, a weighted continuum comparison bounds the actual source-field correlator. All six instantaneous
phase rates remain positive and below the bare gap throughout one bare cycle. The resulting phase coordinate reparameterizes
the complete joint action, retaining the even source energy, both counterterms, and the Berry one-form.

1. The physical question and its inputs

the interacting system.
Here the observable is a bounded source amplitude whose
equation contains a joint source–field expectation. The source
spectrum fixes the signed lane coupling; the receiving field supplies the correlation that changes the clock rate. The analysis
then compares the full continuum trajectory with a specifically
prepared reference trajectory in the same field realization. Controlling the difference between those trajectories gives a bound
on the correlation and, through the exact clock equation, a
uniform bound on the actual phase rate.
The steps have different responsibilities. Sections 2–4 establish the source incidence, the complete pair space and the
normalization. Section 5 constructs the joint dynamics and the
weighted field pairings that make its continuum expressions
meaningful. Section 6 develops the reference comparison and
the six lane certificates. Section 7 changes the parameter of the
complete action using the resulting phase. The conclusion is
a source-to-clock result for the declared receiving model and
preparation.
Each certificate concerns one separately prepared lane. The
six results do not assert that the phase of an arbitrary coherent
combination of lane amplitudes is monotone: interference can
change that combined observable. Likewise, the model-time
rate becomes a physical inverse-seconds rate only after the
stated time assignment is supplied. These distinctions fix which
clock has actually been constructed.

An original Write is a signed event in an ordered source history.
A receiving field observes specified combinations of that source.
Chapter I asks how the original phase incidence, a complete finite source, and a declared field law combine into an interacting
action with a usable local phase clock.
Three layers carry different authority. Original rules supply
the signed Writes, lifted phases, retained tensor map, and source
histories. Receiving laws specify the quadrupole bulk field,
its quantization, the boundary incidence, and the preparation.
Derived compositions include the source spectrum, conserved
charge, actual clock equation, and certified phase reparameterization. An exact composition keeps its inputs identifiable.
[1-4]
The construction uses the full source space C4 ⊗ C4 and
both real field polarizations. All field frequencies and photon
sectors belong to the model. The six clock certificates concern
six separately prepared lanes. Each certificate carries its own
signed root difference, coupling, and hard-branch preparation.
The numerical example receives the unit-strength source
chart, the retained boundary radius, and a capacity-normalized
model time. A physical exchange strength, the reference capacity and its role, the Write-to-seconds assignment, and the
incidence between the source sphere and field boundary remain
explicit physical inputs. No inverse-seconds rate is selected by
the normalized calculation.
How the source-to-clock argument is organized

2. Lifted phases and history

A phase becomes a useful local clock only when three separate
questions have answers. The phase must belong to an identified
physical observable. That observable must remain nonzero so
that its argument can be followed continuously. Finally, its
phase must advance with a rate that does not vanish or change
sign on the interval being used. A frequency written into a
Hamiltonian does not by itself answer all three questions for

A phase can be recorded in several ways. A wrapped phase
specifies a point on the unit circle, represented by eiφ . A lifted
phase is a real number obtained after choosing an initial branch
and following the accumulated phase without reducing it modulo 2π. The lift therefore retains winding information that the
wrapped value discards. An ordered Write history additionally
records which signed events occurred and in what order. These

4. Source energy and the time chart
An energy normalization requires both an operator and a state
in which to evaluate it. The placement basis specifies how
the source is initially selected, while the spectral basis of Q
specifies how that selected state is resolved into eigenvectors.
A placement-basis state will generally be a superposition in the
spectral basis. Its energy expectation is the weighted mean of its
possible energy values; an eigenenergy is the value associated
with a state of sharp energy. The distinction can be checked
quantitatively by the variance.

6. The actual interacting clock
The clock is the phase of a bounded source amplitude evaluated
in the evolving joint state. Its rate receives the field through a
joint correlation. We first derive that equation, then compare the
actual evolution with an exactly specified hard-field reference.
The comparison controls the instantaneous rate throughout a
finite interval and supplies the monotone coordinate used in the
action.

SAM VOLUME I

Retention, accumulation,
and the finite ledger
Chapter II • Source-to-field companion update
Sean Brady
Originator and conceptual director
OpenAI ChatGPT and Codex • Research collaborators and co-authors
15 October 2026

Abstract. A retained account can outlast its present address. Original Write, interacting-clock, spin and outgoing-field results
distinguish predictive state, timed history and energetic complement. This development adds source-linked spectral predictions,
compact memory and monitor derivations, exact finite-source nonclosure certificates, a worked paid-reference protocol, and
an eight-time ensemble measurement with explicit apparatus and sampling budgets. Signed phases, full source energy and
physical calibration remain in the same account. A companion source-to-field extension separates complete energy from a
diagnostic minimum, gives exact spatial receiving constructions, and derives an operational coupling-response criterion for the
actual interacting clock.

1. The physical proposition

direction. Reordering closed blocks changes when a response
occurs while preserving its whole-history occupancy. [3]
The eight immediate outputs in this assay and the eight partition addresses introduced later have separate source definitions.
Their equal cardinalities supply no transition map.
Chapter I contributes another exact distinction. Its four equaloccupation source eigenstates have zero D and C currents while
carrying different energies. A current record therefore leaves an
energetic complement. A complete energy receiver must retain
that complement even when the current is zero. [2]
The task is consequently to specify the record needed by the
chosen future receiver, then carry its physical account through
an actual evolution.

SAM begins with matter displacing substrate and the displaced
account being retained. The aquarium thought experiment
makes this relation visible: an object appearing in a filled enclosure changes the surrounding arrangement. Its physical content
is the requirement to account for the consequence and its later
reception. A fluid equation is an additional model choice. [1]
The recent work lets us ask this more precisely. What must a
Write leave behind so that its consequence remains available to
a later interaction? A present reading, a persistent source state,
an ordered history, and an outgoing field can retain different
parts of that account.
This chapter uses an operational distinction: two histories
remain distinguishable when a specified permitted continuation
gives different receiver outputs. This defines what a receiving
description must preserve. It does not assign a measured energy
or a spatial density to information alone.
The finite ledger organizes the available types. Its physical
payload is developed through the source, evolution, reference
and receiver that consume it.

3. Predictive equivalence and retention
For a fixed source, event alphabet and receiver, let O(h; u) denote the output obtained by extending history h with an allowed
future word u. Define
h ∼ h0

⇐⇒

O(h; u) = O(h0 ; u) for all u.

This relation is preserved by appending the same event: each
subsequent test is already a permitted continuation. A quotient
state can therefore preserve every future output when its classes

38. Pay for the controller
The specified waveform is an externally driven instrument. A
material autonomous controller must produce its schedule, store
or recover work and retain the phase-turn record. When coupled
to the quantum source or reference it can also become entangled;
the enlarged Hamiltonian then determines the clock and energy
account.
The protocol has made the required work exchange finite
and explicit. It has not assigned a cost to original source actuation, waveform generation, qubit preparation, readout rotations,
detector reset, external-counter memory or cooling. Their physical models supply those further payments. Recovering equal
positive and negative reference work does not determine their
dissipation.
For the protected-coherence experiment, the independent
common calibration fixes gH through Ξ and fixes ε through one
absolute scale. The two-frequency record is then a prediction.
Its source-guided cadence and apparatus tolerances specify
what a proposed implementation must deliver.
These are concrete construction tasks with quantitative targets. They can receive hardware and channel assignments while
preserving the original signed source response, phase lift, full
field and energetic complement. [12]

fiber (−1, 0); both are single accepted port flips. z0 and z1

nonnegative squares and cannot lower the attained fixed-outside

Abstract. A retained energy account becomes a spatial field through a specified localization, coupling and receiving operator.
This chapter develops the isolated Poisson kernel, its energy and force proofs, and two complete finite constructions: the actual
retained eight-site source profile under a declared physical embedding, and an exactly solvable shell network with boundary
and continuum errors. A static Chapter I field-energy example and an exact interacting-clock coupling criterion connect the
construction to Chapters I and II. Source identities, physical assignments and computed results are stated separately. All earlier
drafts remain preserved.

4.4 A durable accessible record is an operational claim
A useful record definition specifies more than entanglement.
Let {I j } be a quantum instrument: each map is completely
positive and trace non-increasing, and ∑ j I j is trace preserving. Its probabilities are p j = Tr I j (ρ), and its conditional
output is I j (ρ)/p j for p j > 0. The instrument can describe
a declared path-marking task, but must not be read as establishing a pre-existing route value in every coherent preparation.
If only selected outcomes are retained, the omitted outcomes
must remain in the complete instrument; renormalizing the retained branch describes postselection, not a new unconditional
probability law.

4.5 Controls and the boundary of the claim
The preceding equations prescribe concrete wrong-controls.
Treating a marker-only rotation as a joint inverse incorrectly predicts an unconditional restored fringe. Tracing out an
orthogonal environmental marker and then declaring it absent incorrectly reinstates coherence. Sorting eraser outcomes
and comparing that conditional visibility with unsorted whichway data mixes ensembles. Treating D as marker-acquired
information without subtracting or reporting prior predictability
misreads biased preparations. Treating a returned local state
as a globally erased event discards the history carrier. Finally,
labelling a reduced density matrix as one selected outcome
imports an additional postulate without saying so.
These controls are standard quantum benchmarks. They
discipline the route/write terminology and identify what an
executable substrate account must reproduce. No new SAM
prediction follows from renaming the instrument outcome a
write. Such a prediction would require an additional, quantitatively specified dynamics or access rule, its parameter domain,

here. We must name the restored subsystem, the other degrees
of freedom, and the operations by which a record can be read.

SAM VOLUME I

Horizon thermodynamics and accessible information
Chapter VII
Sean Brady
Originator and conceptual director
Research development with OpenAI ChatGPT and Codex
Unified expanded edition | 19 October 2026

Abstract. The completed boundary connects exterior geometry, finite thermodynamics, and accessible records. This chapter
derives the surface gravity and first law under the explicitly inherited metric, temperature, and quarter-area premises; develops
exact finite-entry transitions, their Catalan expansion, and conditional detailed balance; and separates thermal occupation
from an absolute emission rate. The retained Si29 calculation is reformulated as a Hessian-level obstruction to scalar area–
information proportionality, while its entropy–area pair provides local coordinates on the specified two-parameter source
family. New analytic checks clarify finite-capacity errors, transmitted count fluctuations, entropy balance, and the distinction
between a causal horizon and a material surface. The remaining physical joins are stated as testable tasks: a source-selected
boundary response, energy and clock calibration, species-resolved dynamics, a certified information map, and consistency with
compact-surface observations. No new native source execution or absolute luminosity is claimed.

1. Purpose, premises, and the boundary question

1.1 Evidence levels

The unit-accumulation surface joins three subjects that must
remain logically distinct: exterior geometry, thermodynamic
bookkeeping, and accessible information. Chapter V supplies a
static exterior adapter and an exact finite ledger. Chapter VI supplies the operational meaning of a record and the contraction of
distinguishability under restricted access. This chapter assembles those results, extends their elementary consequences, and
identifies the additional physical input needed for an absolute
radiation law.
The principal outcome is conditional but precise. Given the
Schwarzschild exterior adapter, the usual normalization of time
at infinity, the Hawking temperature conversion, and the retained quarter-area entropy rule, the horizon temperature and
differential first law agree with semiclassical black-hole thermodynamics. Given the integer-entry continuation, the exact
energy of a finite emission follows algebraically. Neither statement derives the adapter, the quarter-area rule, or an emission
clock from the microscopic source. Keeping these dependencies visible prevents an agreement inherited from an input from
being counted a second time as an independent prediction.
The finite Si29 example provides a different kind of result.
Its reported relative-entropy Hessian is not proportional to its
enclosing-area Hessian, and entropy together with area locally
distinguishes two source directions. This is a useful obstruction
to a particular finite-source information map. It is not a disproof
of a continuum horizon identity formulated for a different area,
state family, and perturbation order.
Throughout this chapter, A(r) denotes dimensionless accumulation, AH denotes physical horizon area, and N denotes the
dimensionless entropy-entry count. These are different objects.
In particular, A(rH ) = 1 does not mean that the physical area is
one square metre or one Planck area. Entropies written as s are
dimensionless, with physical entropy S = kB s. This convention
keeps logarithmic quantum-information expressions separate
from thermodynamic units.

Four levels of statement recur. An input is an adopted bridge
or constitutive premise. A conditional derivation follows from
such inputs by explicit mathematics. A retained calculation is
reported in the supplied source record but has not been rerun
here. An open closure is a missing physical map, experiment,
or computation. The expanded calculations below are analytic
consequences of printed premises; they are not new native
source runs.
The closure surface also requires a causal interpretation. The
divergence of a static coordinate travel time does not by itself
prove that an infaller cannot cross a regular horizon. In the
adopted metric, radial free-fall trajectories can reach the horizon
in finite proper time. SAM’s rule about completion of the
parent ledger therefore needs its own operational statement:
which event, record, or custody transfer is forbidden, and with
respect to which observer? A restriction on exterior record
access is weaker than a reflecting material wall. The distinction
will matter both for radiation and for observational limits on
compact surfaces.

12.2 Why two coordinates do not imply complete recovery
The qubit example also clarifies local information maps. Let
a hypothetical scalar readout be a = a0 + αx + β z, and pair it
with the entropy s(r). The Jacobian of (s, a) with respect to
(x, z) has determinant proportional to β x − αz away from r = 0.
It is locally invertible where that expression is nonzero and the
entropy radial derivative is nonzero. At the maximally mixed
reference the entropy gradient vanishes, so the determinant vanishes even though the relative-entropy Hessian remains positive
definite.
Thus a positive information metric does not guarantee that
any arbitrarily chosen pair of observables is a valid coordinate chart. Conversely, a valid local chart on a restricted twoparameter family does not reconstruct an arbitrary quantum
state. Allowing a σy component would introduce a third direction not covered by those two scalar readouts. The Si29 inverse
should be understood with precisely the same discipline: its
claim concerns the supplied two-direction family near specified
reference points.
The distinction between local coordinates and global recovery is also topological. Even a nonzero Jacobian on a small
region does not prevent distant points from sharing the same
observable pair. Phase periodicity and discrete symmetries can
create multiple branches. A boundary-information claim therefore needs both a local stability bound and a domain statement.
Without the latter, an inverse used to reconstruct a source could
silently return the wrong branch while fitting both measured
scalars.
These examples turn the chapter’s information language into
concrete operations: state preparation, restriction, measurement,
conditioning, and reconstruction. They show what accessibility
can remove, what an inverse can recover, and which claims
require additional dimensions or dynamics. They do not identify
inaccessible information with annihilated information, nor do
they establish recovery from an evaporating horizon. Those
stronger questions require the source-selected global channel
that remains to be derived.

A proposed horizon channel must pass checks beyond fitting
one occupation law. It should map every allowed input density
operator to a positive output with unit trace, including inputs
entangled with a reference system. That stronger requirement
is why complete positivity, rather than positivity only on an
isolated subsystem, is the appropriate channel condition. A
formula verified on diagonal occupation mixtures may fail on
coherent superpositions or reference-entangled states.
Energy accounting must also be stated at the channel level.
An apparently passive exterior map can exchange energy with
unobserved boundary degrees of freedom, so the channel’s dilation or an equivalent work-and-heat account is needed before
claiming that it conserves energy. If the map is explicitly time
dependent, the control mechanism can perform work. Such
work cannot be omitted merely because the exterior output
resembles a thermal state.
For a family of stationary scattering channels, analyticity and
causality constrain the frequency response. Choosing a separate
transmission number at every frequency without a causal response function can reproduce a desired spectrum while failing
to define a physical time-domain evolution. Likewise, demanding unit transmission in one calculation and perfect reflection
in another is not a single boundary theory. The response has to
be compatible across the observables to which it is applied.
These conditions provide practical rejection tests for future
completions. A map producing a negative eigenvalue on an
allowed input is invalid. A channel that emits more energy
than the source loses without identifying an external reservoir
has an incomplete account. A response whose chosen boundary condition cannot generate the claimed scattering solution
must be revised before interpreting its poles or flux. None of
these tests depends on agreement with a particular astronomical dataset; they are internal requirements for a well-defined
physical model.

The parentheses matter. Both the linear and quadratic terms

There are two scientifically different possibilities. The refinement could be an observational response operator mapping
one underlying density to an effective measured parameter. Alternatively it could be a second candidate background model
with a different matter density. The first possibility requires an
explicit forward map from the clean state to each observable.
The second requires separate predictions and separate statistical
scores. Neither permits selecting whichever number agrees
better with each dataset after inspecting its residual.
For the expanded volume, the clean packet is the default
structural ledger. The effective packet remains a separately
named conditional lane. A calculation that uses it must state the
input, the operator’s scope, and the associated complement. The
common road amplitude remains RA0 unless the road operator
itself is independently changed. These conventions preserve the
original distinction while preventing silent movement between
ledgers.
Holding Ωb and the thermal conversion fixed leaves H0 unchanged in this particular refinement. It does not leave H(z), the
age, growth, matter-radiation equality, or the distance-redshift
relation unchanged. Those depend on the matter row and must
be recomputed. The importance of the distinction is therefore
physical, even though the Hubble cascade itself is unchanged.

9. Selection, enumeration, and honest comparison
9.1 What the closing review establishes
The closing review reports a grammar enumeration with multiplicative expressions 2a 3b 7c π d . Its smallest stated ranges are
|a| ≤ 8, |b| ≤ 6, |c| ≤ 1, and |d| ≤ 4, giving 17 · 13 · 3 · 9 = 5967
exponent tuples. In that enumeration it reports 14 expressions in a one-standard-deviation matter window, 14 in a baryon
window, and six in an η10 window. These are retained review
results, not independently reproduced enumeration outputs in
this chapter.
Several qualifications are essential. The target windows and
their units must be explicit: η10 = 1010 η is not the same numerical target as η. Additive expressions such as 2A0 (1 − χ)
are not members of the purely multiplicative base grammar,
although multiplicative competitors can land near their target
value. Counting tuples is not necessarily counting distinct numerical expressions if a richer grammar admits identities. And
the fraction of a finite arbitrary list landing inside a window is
not automatically a probability or a statistical significance.
The review’s wider grammars admit larger exponents, named
additive factors, and half-integer powers. Their increasing
match counts demonstrate that a match’s impressiveness depends on the available search space. They do not determine the

relative to a critical density proportional to H02 . A theory that
rejects that critical-density relation cannot retain this Hubble
inference unchanged. Likewise, the calculation uses measured
dimensionful constants as well as one measured cosmological
thermal anchor. “One anchor” means one cosmological calibration in this chain, not an absence of external metrology or
physical assumptions.

9.2 A prospective protocol

11. A complement is not yet dark-energy dynamics

A usable protocol has four stages. First, publish the admissible operations and the physical rule selecting each expression.
Second, freeze the clean or effective interpretation and every
downstream bridge. Third, compute observables on an identified dataset not used to choose the expression. Fourth, report the
full residual vector and covariance without revising the grammar in response. A failed prediction can motivate a revised
model, but the revision should receive a new version and a new
prospective test.
This approach preserves a real advantage of a small grammar:
a frozen packet imposes correlations across observables. It also
prevents those correlations from being overstated. If H0 is
calculated from η and Ωb , agreement of all three is not three
independent miracles. Their joint significance depends on the
data covariance and on which quantities participated in the
original selection.

Setting a ledger remainder equal to 1 − Ωm supplies a number, not an equation of state. In a conventional homogeneous
background,

At z = 0, exact closure requires Ωr0 + Ωm0 + Ωk0 + ΩX0 = 1.
Thus in a spatially flat radiation-aware implementation the physical complement is ΩX0 = 1 − Ωm0 − Ωr0 , with neutrinos counted consistently between the matter and radiation terms. The
clean ledger’s 1−Ωm is a late-time radiation-neglecting complement unless an alternative accounting convention is explicitly
adopted. Radiation is numerically small today but essential for
Chapter IX and cannot be silently counted twice.
If redshift is attributed in part to a propagation mechanism,
the model must predict the transformation of photon energies,
arrival intervals, solid angles, and number flux together. Matching a luminosity-distance curve alone does not establish consistency with time dilation, temperature evolution, or distance
duality. In the standard metric, photon-conserving case the
latter reads DL = (1 + z)2 DA . A replacement road law must
specify which hypotheses it changes and produce a new joint
test rather than inherit this relation selectively.

10. Observational placement
Planck’s published base-ΛCDM inference gives H0 = 67.4 ±
0.5 km s−1 Mpc−1 and Ωm = 0.315±0.007 [VIII.2]. With those
rounded comparator values, the clean inventory differs by about
−0.30 standard deviations in H0 and +0.47 in Ωm , treating
the SAM point as fixed for this descriptive calculation. These
are model-dependent posterior comparisons, not direct measurements of bare substrate quantities, and they are not an
independent joint likelihood.
The original draft also compared H0 with the SH0ES value
73.04 ± 1.04 km s−1 Mpc−1 [VIII.3]. The inventory’s lower value is a commitment of its frozen chain. It does not resolve the
discrepancy by agreeing with one side. Any proposed resolution
must propagate the same cosmology into distance calibration,
selection effects, stellar standardization, and the observables
used by the relevant analysis.
DESI DR2 supplies an important later test [VIII.4]. Its primary paper finds that the preferred flat-ΛCDM parameters depend
on the selected data combination and that allowing evolving
dark energy changes the interpretation. The closing review’s
provisional Ωm ≃ 0.303 ± 0.004 was explicitly marked for verification. It is not promoted here into a universal DESI number
or a definitive exclusion significance. A valid comparison must
name the exact likelihood combination, neutrino assumptions,
dark-energy model, and posterior statistic. The clean and effective inventories should then be scored separately against the
same setup.
The literature placement is therefore clear without a broad
originality claim. Standard analyses infer cosmological parameters from a specified dynamical model and data likelihood.
This inventory proposes algebraic restrictions on several of
those parameters and then tests the restricted packet. Its distinctive proposal is the particular substrate-to-density assignment.

13. Independent abundance tests and a reproducible input manifest
The abundance rule becomes most valuable when it commits
to a calculation that did not choose its coefficients. Primordial
nucleosynthesis is a natural candidate because the baryon-tophoton ratio affects nuclear reaction competition in an expanding plasma. The calculation also depends on the expansion
history, neutron lifetime, effective relativistic content, and laboratory reaction rates. Holding only η fixed while adjusting
those quantities to force agreement would not be a clean test of
the proposed packet.
A prospective abundance analysis should therefore begin
with a written input manifest. The manifest specifies whether η
refers to the post-electron-annihilation photon bath, which neutrino temperature and effective species count are adopted, and
whether the standard thermal relation between cosmic time and
temperature is used. It records the treatment of nuclear binding
in the baryon mass conversion and distinguishes that conversion from the baryon number that enters reaction equations. It
identifies the reaction-rate compilation and its covariance, since
several yields share rate uncertainties.
The principal outputs are element abundances with uncertainty budgets separated into nuclear, observational, and cosmological components. Deuterium is useful because its surviving
abundance responds strongly to the baryon density, but a numerical scaling law should be obtained from the selected network
over its stated range rather than imported without verification.
Helium supplies a complementary sensitivity to the expansion
and weak-interaction history. Lithium should be reported as
well, even where the standard calculation and astrophysical
inference have known difficulties; selective reporting of only
favorable elements would defeat the prospective protocol.
No BBN network was executed for this expansion. The
purpose of the specification is to prevent an analytic inventory

14. Worked dimensional conversion and unit
checks
A numerical cascade is easiest to audit when each step
has a dimensional meaning. The independent arithmetic
check accompanying this chapter uses c = 299792458 m s−1 ,
kB = 1.380649 × 10−23 J K−1 , h̄ = 1.054571817 × 10−34 J s,
G = 6.67430×10−11 m3 kg−1 s−2 , and m p = 1.67262192595×
10−27 kg. These are the chosen numerical inputs to this check,
with the displayed rounding of h̄; they are not an independent determination of the constants. The length conversion is
1 Mpc = 3.085677581491367 × 1022 m.
The ratio kB T0 /(h̄c) has units of inverse length. Cubing it and
multiplying by 2ζ (3)/π 2 therefore gives a number per cubic
metre. The result is 4.10726849 × 108 m−3 , which becomes
410.726849 cm−3 because one cubic metre contains one million
cubic centimetres. Losing that conversion factor would corrupt
every subsequent density by six orders of magnitude while
leaving all dimensionless inventory identities untouched.
Next, H100 = 105 /(3.085677581491367 × 1022 ) s−1 . Its
square divided by G has units of mass density, as required
for ρcrit,100 . The factor K divides that mass density by m p nγ ,
another mass density, and is therefore dimensionless. Finally, η/K is a dimensionless physical baryon density parameter,

The inferred baryon number density is approximately
0.2504 m−3 in this convention. It is an average over cosmological volume, not the density in stars, gas clouds, or galaxies.
Multiplying by m p produces a mean baryonic mass density of
order 4.19 × 10−28 kg m−3 . Dividing that result by the critical

The independent script checks this closure in both directions.
There are therefore two equivalent paths through the conversion. One computes K, then ωb , then h. The other uses
equation (27) directly. Agreement between the paths is an implementation check because the same algebra underlies both.
It is not a second observational constraint. A useful release
should nevertheless retain both paths: one is convenient for
cosmological-code inputs and the other exposes dimensional
dependencies.
The calculation also shows why the proton-mass approximation deserves explicit treatment. Baryon number counts nucleons, whereas mass density includes the composition-dependent
energy of bound nuclei and associated electrons according to
the adopted convention. A future high-precision implementation should compute mb from the same primordial composition
used in the thermal calculation. Replacing m p by that mean
mass changes H0 by the square root of their ratio. This correction can be calculated once the composition convention is
fixed; it should not be treated as an arbitrary nuisance parameter
selected to move the expansion rate toward an observational
preference.

10.95. These examples make the physical leverage of the selected ingredients visible. They do not claim those alternatives
are plausible cosmologies; their purpose is to show that “no
continuous fit” does not mean “no consequential choice.”
The exercise can be made into an auditable selection test
by declaring a comparator interval before evaluating the nine
entries. The number landing inside the interval then has a
definite meaning for this set. It still does not become a universal
false-alarm probability, because the set was not drawn from
a physical probability distribution and does not include all
conceivable expressions. Expanding the grammar after seeing
that count changes the experiment. A defensible significance
calculation would require an explicit prior over the alternatives
or a prospective predictive score.
A role-sensitive derivation could make eight of the nine candidates inadmissible for structural reasons. For example, a
demonstrated six-stage independent transfer law could select
the exponent before any cosmological target is consulted. A
conservation theorem could select the weight. If those arguments are supplied, the numerical comparison becomes much
stronger because the expression is no longer selected by its
agreement. The present chapter identifies those possible forms
of explanation without inventing the missing theorem.
The same logic applies to the clean and effective matter rows.
Treating them as two prespecified hypotheses is legitimate.
Moving between them separately for Planck, BAO, halos, and
fate introduces an undeclared selection at every comparison.
A bounded diagnostic should therefore print both complete
prediction vectors and apply one scoring rule to each, rather
than construct a favorable hybrid after inspecting residuals.

The example is useful as a baseline because it creates a
full function H(z) from a small packet and a clear dynamical
law. It also makes circularity easy to identify. Agreement
with a standard-background age after importing the standard
background is a consistency check of the restricted parameter
packet. A genuinely new substrate prediction would require
deriving or modifying the background law and carrying that
modification through distances, growth, and thermal history.
No numerical age is used as a new observational claim
here. The companion check evaluates the integral’s closed form
and the acceleration expression for audit purposes. Radiation,
massive-neutrino evolution, and any evolving dark component
are omitted by construction. A precision comparison must restore them or bound their effects, rather than present the simple

For residual vector (1, 1) the quadratic score is 2/(1 + ρ); for
(1, −1) it is 2/(1 − ρ). At ρ = 0.8, these are approximately
1.111 and 10, although each individual residual has magnitude
one. Ignoring covariance would assign both the value two. A
comparison that reports only a list of separate sigma offsets
cannot distinguish these cases.
The physical interpretation is straightforward. Positively correlated data commonly move together, so a common-direction
displacement is relatively unsurprising. A displacement in opposite directions fights that correlation and is more strongly
penalized. Cosmological parameter posteriors and overlapping
sky measurements contain precisely this kind of structure, albeit
in much larger spaces. It is therefore inappropriate to multiply
separate agreement probabilities or add individually quoted
sigma values to summarize the inventory’s success.
A complete test should operate as close as practical to the
actual observable data vector. If compressed parameter posteriors are used instead, their model dependence, covariance,
and prior information must be retained. The comparison should
also distinguish a fixed prediction from a model whose nuisance
quantities were optimized. The number of displayed identities
does not determine the effective number of independent tests.

17.1 An explicit audit of shared information
The conditional background example makes it possible to assign
each conclusion to its actual inputs. The matter fraction uses
the floor and the chosen density identification. The baryon
fraction uses the allocation rule. The baryon-to-photon ratio
uses the container weight and exponent. The Hubble constant
then uses those quantities plus the thermal and critical-density
bridges. The age uses the Hubble constant, matter fraction,
and an additional expansion law. These dependencies form a
directed graph rather than a list of independent successes.
If the same observed CMB posterior helped select the matter
rule, baryon allocation, and abundance expression, agreement
of the derived age with an age inferred from that posterior is
especially correlated. It can expose a transcription error or an
inconsistent conversion, but it cannot honestly be counted as a
wholly new observation predicted without contact with the data.
The route to additional evidence is to test a consequence whose
relevant information did not participate in the selections.
There are different strengths of such a test. Reusing the
same sky with a different statistic can check an aspect not explicitly fitted, but shared cosmic variance and selection history
remain. A different instrument provides different systematics
while often measuring the same underlying realization. A lightelement abundance or a local distance measurement probes
different physical processes, yet still brings model and calibration assumptions. Independence is a graded property to be
documented, not a label supplied by a new filename.
This audit also prevents excessive pessimism. A selected
expression can become useful when it survives increasingly
demanding, genuinely frozen tests. The appropriate record
is a sequence of versioned hypotheses and their results. The
inventory is not disqualified because its first identification was
retrospective; it is simply required to earn prospective status
through the next tests. Publishing dependencies and rejected
alternatives makes that transition visible to a reader.

18. Results, open closures, and failure conditions

These records are cited as source provenance, not as newly
executed evidence.

The completed arithmetic establishes exact conditional identities for the clean inventory, its baryonic fraction, the container
expression for η, and the thermal conversion to H0 . The formal dimensional cancellation is valid within its fixed angular
convention. The finite differences between clean and effective
matter rows are explicit. Sensitivity derivatives identify how
changes propagate. These are the mathematical closures added
here.
Three physical derivations remain central. The baryon allocation needs a measure and a selection theorem for (1 − χ). The
abundance needs a mechanism selecting the sixth power and
the 7/4 weight. The cosmological bridge needs a dynamical
interpretation of density, critical density, and the complement.
None is supplied by repeating an exact decimal match.
Three tests are particularly useful. A frozen BBN calculation
tests the abundance outside the original parameter matching,
provided reaction rates and their uncertainties are propagated.
A single distance and recombination calculation tests whether
one expansion-rate ledger can serve all lanes. A specified latetime w(z) or native road law tests the complement’s physical
interpretation using joint distance and timing observables. Each
can fail while the algebra remains correct; that is what makes
the physical assignment empirical.
Failure should be recorded at the level of the affected claim.
A discrepancy in deuterium could challenge the abundance or
thermal assumptions without invalidating 126/72 = 7/4. A
distance mismatch could challenge the expansion history rather
than the photon integral. A lack of unique selection would
weaken predictive status while leaving a useful phenomenological parametrization. The distinction between arithmetic
truth, conditional modeling, and observational adequacy is the
organizing discipline of this chapter.

Abstract. This chapter expands the thermal-history and microwave-background test of the selected SAM inventory. It separates

comparisons. The native receipt remains a percent-level calculation with documented atomic and time-variable corrections.
The full-shape receipts are compatibility checks of a selected packet under inherited transfer physics, rather than independent
derivations of that physics. The published second-peak comparator is corrected, and the ACT temperature residual is retained
explicitly. New analytical diagnostics distinguish moving recombination endpoints from background-integral changes and show
why a visibility peak alone cannot certify the entire ionization history. No historical simulation or likelihood is rerun in this
expansion; the numerical execution evidence still required is listed alongside clear validation and failure conditions.

The cosmic microwave background tests several parts of a cosmological account at once. Its angular spectra depend on the
expansion history, the inertia of the photon–baryon fluid, the
ionization history, the gravitational evolution of perturbations,
and the projection of those perturbations onto the sky. Agreement with a density fraction alone therefore does not establish
agreement with the microwave sky. Conversely, a successful calculation using an established transfer solver is evidence
about the supplied parameter packet; it is not automatically a
derivation of the transfer physics from the substrate.
This chapter retains the original distinction between two
lanes. The native lane is the program’s internally implemented hydrogen recombination and optical-depth calculation, anchored by the reported record CR001c@19. The word native
identifies the implementation and its upstream inventory; it
does not mean that the Peebles atomic model or its rate coefficients have been derived from SAM. The full-shape lane
passes the selected cosmological packet to standard recombination and CAMB. Its reported Planck and ACT comparisons
test the propagation of that packet through established thermal
and perturbation physics. Both lanes are informative, but they
answer different questions.

8. Selection, likelihoods, and a decisive validation
program

A useful error budget separates numerical error, atomicmodel truncation, uncertain empirical rate inputs, background
assumptions, and selector uncertainty. Tight solver tolerances
address only the first. The many digits printed in a selected
identity describe arithmetic precision, not demonstrated physical accuracy. Similarly, a percent-level recombination residual
cannot be called a precision success merely because it is small
on a plot.
The chapter therefore establishes a disciplined intermediate
position. The reported packet propagates through standard thermal physics with promising spectrum-level comparisons, and
the internally implemented hydrogen lane provides a concrete
route for improving the native account. The remaining tasks are
sharply defined: derive or explicitly inherit the thermal processes, settle the ruler, expose the likelihood evidence, and replace
perturbation selectors with a governing calculation. Until then
the full-shape lane is a compatibility result under established
physics and the native lane is a partially completed transport
model.

The original packet lies near the Planck posterior by construction or selection history. Good spectra under the same standard
transfer physics are consequently expected to a substantial degree. They remain useful checks of compatibility and implementation, but should not be counted as a wholly independent
discovery on top of parameter agreement. A small set of wellmotivated discrete choices may eventually be compelling; the
relevant evidence requires the allowed grammar, its physical
restrictions, the candidates considered, and the information
available when each was selected.

An executable thermal result should be recoverable from a

numerical tolerances, integration interval, transition criteria,

Three independent checks are particularly economical. First,

The matching-reference experiment should retain residual
curves rather than only maximum differences. A broad coherent
bias suggests a different rate convention or background input;
an isolated discontinuity suggests a switch or interpolation artifact; oscillatory differences that shrink with refinement suggest
numerical error. These are diagnostic hypotheses to test, not
guaranteed classifications. The purpose is to make the next
correction attributable and reproducible.
Finally, a failed comparison should have a declared disposition. A numerical failure requires a corrected implementation
and a fresh receipt. A mismatch caused by inherited atomic approximations limits the native lane. A discrepancy that remains
after matched inputs, converged numerics, and validated atomic
physics is evidence against the selected cosmological packet or
its assumed background. The chapter becomes stronger when
these possibilities are distinguished before the result is known.

9.2 Visibility width and information beyond one epoch
A peak redshift compresses a whole distribution into one number. Two ionization histories can share the same z∗ while having different widths or residual ionization tails. Those histories need not have the same diffusion damping or polarization
source. A native calculation should therefore publish xe (a)
and the normalized visibility array, not merely its maximum.
Useful diagnostics include the mean and variance with respect
to the chosen probability measure and the integrated late-time
visibility contribution.
This recommendation follows from a simple mathematical
fact: fixing the location of a maximum imposes only one local
condition on a function. It leaves infinitely many functions
with different integrals and widths. Agreement in z∗ therefore
cannot certify agreement in a line-of-sight integral weighted by
that function. The same logic applies to matching a drag epoch
without checking the preceding drag history.
A controlled numerical test can deliberately perturb the ionization history in a narrow redshift interval while holding its
peak position nearly fixed. Passing that history to a transfer
calculation then measures which angular scales respond. Such
an experiment diagnoses sensitivity; it does not establish that
the perturbation corresponds to valid atomic physics. Physical changes must come from rate equations with a consistent

measurement alone.

11.2 Photon heating requires both energy and number accounting

This elementary result explains why a near-unity average of
pointwise residual squares cannot replace a full covariance likelihood. Calibration and foreground uncertainties can introduce
structured directions in data space. Marginalizing a nuisance
parameter that shifts both points together may further reduce
sensitivity to the common residual while leaving the opposing
residual prominent. A model comparison must identify which
directions were fitted, integrated over, or held fixed.
The example also separates two uses of a reference cosmology. A frozen reference produces a residual statistic under
exactly the same nuisance policy as the SAM packet. An optimized reference has spent additional freedom to lower its
statistic. Both comparisons may be useful, but they answer different questions. Reporting the raw difference, the optimization
or marginalization policy, and the parameter dimension is more
informative than attaching the phrase “no optimizer” to one
model alone. No two-point toy calculation supplies the missing
Planck or ACT likelihood; it demonstrates why their complete
definitions are necessary.

The purpose of the balance equations is to make any proposed

Even perfect numerical convergence leaves the physical approximation intact. A converged hydrogen-only effective atom
remains hydrogen-only. A converged inherited perturbation
hierarchy remains inherited. A converged likelihood evaluated

should never be used to suggest that a selected physical interpretation has been proved by additional digits.

Many-source accumulation and galaxy halos
Chapter X

Research development with OpenAI ChatGPT and Codex

Abstract. This chapter develops the many-source accumulation account of galaxy support. It preserves the reported SPARC
results while separating potential lifts, radial force, and geometry-dependent mass inference. The proposed coordinate 10/π is
analyzed as a population identification, with explicit treatment of selection history, uncertainty, and the algebraic dependence of
the mass-ratio statistic. A radial organization law and an untouched-sample test remain necessary for a predictive halo theory.
The reported support deficit, radial randomization results, and outer mass assignment are preserved with their original receipt
identifiers. New derivations expose which results share the same underlying statistic, quantify the approximate resolution of the
population median, and constrain admissible radial profiles through density positivity. Disk geometry, stellar mass-to-light ratios,
correlated observational uncertainties, and the distinction between measured-radius and virial masses are treated explicitly. The
constituent interpretation is kept separate from the gravitational support measurement. No SPARC replay or new halo-formation
simulation is claimed; the chapter ends with a prospective protocol and falsifiable requirements for a completed organization
law.

1. Inventory is not a halo profile

2. The many-source field and the force readout

A cosmic inventory specifies how much of a component exists
on average. A rotation curve specifies the radial gravitational
support required in one galaxy. Connecting them requires a
distribution law. The identity Ωc = Ωm − Ωb cannot, by itself,
determine a halo radius, a central density, a concentration, or
the relation between a halo and its baryonic disk. This chapter
develops the original many-source accumulation proposal while
making that missing dynamical step explicit.
The empirical starting point is the supplied chapter’s analysis
of SPARC, a public compilation of 175 late-type galaxies with
infrared photometry and resolved rotation curves [X.1]. The reported campaign finds a large baryonic support deficit, a radial
rise in a dimensionless support ratio, and an outer population
centre near 10/π. It also reports a near-unity median for masses
assigned with that coordinate. These results are preserved as
historical receipts. The underlying galaxy tables, cuts, randomization code, and profile parameters were not supplied with this
expansion; no independent SPARC reanalysis is claimed.
Three questions must remain distinct. Does a support deficit
exist under the adopted stellar population and geometry assumptions? Does the selected ratio summarize its population centre?
Does a substrate transport law predict the radial profile and its
galaxy-to-galaxy variation? The first two are empirical or phenomenological questions addressed by the retained campaign.
The third is the outstanding physical closure. Identifying these
levels prevents a successful descriptive coordinate from being
presented as a completed theory of galaxy formation.
The symbol X∞ is retained for continuity with the original
draft, but its present empirical meaning is an outer-sample
coordinate. It has not been established as the mathematical
limit r → ∞ of each galaxy. This distinction becomes essential
when considering finite baryonic mass and approximately flat
rotation curves.

radial force. The enclosed account in Eq. (5) is a force-derived
quantity, not the full potential in Eq. (4).
The superposition law is linear in prescribed source density.
It does not determine that density. A linear Green function
supplies the response to a source; a halo-formation law must
explain the source’s distribution, its conservation, and its equilibrium or time evolution. This is the central dependency
of the chapter. Summing known baryonic lifts cannot create
an unspecified nonbaryonic component merely by changing
notation.

account. CR025@08 introduces a clustered profile and reports
a median rotation-curve RMS falling from 40.95 to 3.63 km s−1 ,
with median overdensity about 7.9 × 104 relative to the cosmic
dark-component mean.
These are distinct conclusions. The bounded subchannel
result excludes that specific allocation as a sufficient explanation within its assumptions; it does not exclude every possible
post-formation mechanism. The improved RMS shows that
the chosen clustered profile can supply the missing support;
without its explicit parameters, priors, and fitting procedure,
it does not establish parameter-free predictive accuracy. The
profile itself must be published before the improvement can be
compared fairly with alternative halo descriptions.

12. An inference ledger for the halo claim
A useful way to organize the remaining work is to track which
inference each observation can support. The observed line-ofsight velocities, distances, and inclinations first determine a
kinematic rotation curve. Photometry and gas maps, combined
with stellar assumptions and geometry, determine the baryonic
contribution. Subtracting the two yields a residual acceleration.
Choosing a halo shape converts that acceleration to a density or
enclosed mass. Choosing a constituent model converts the density to a number of objects or an effective field state. Finally, a
formation model connects that population to the early-universe
inventory. Each arrow adds assumptions, and no agreement at
an earlier arrow eliminates the later ones.
This ledger is especially important when discussing the
phrase “the halo is the cosmic inventory, clustered.” Within a model that identifies the residual with nonbaryonic mass
and retains the standard force law, the phrase is a sensible programmatic statement. It is not a measured identity between
a local rotation-curve residual and the cosmological density
fraction. The local baryon retention efficiency, material outside
the measured radius, halo assembly, and selection of luminous
disks all intervene. A universal cosmic ratio need not be the
ratio inside the last observed radius of every galaxy.
There is also a distinction between an enclosed mass and
a virial mass. Equation (14) applies only inside Rout under
the adopted halo geometry. It does not supply a mass at an
overdensity radius such as R200 . Extrapolating to that radius requires the missing outer profile and a definition of the reference
density. Any comparison with cosmological mass functions or
abundance matching must therefore include the extrapolation
rather than label the measured-radius mass simply “the halo
mass.”
A model with a correct population centre but unmodeled
scatter can still be useful. It provides a baseline against which
to ask whether residuals correlate with independent observables.
If a concentration relation is later proposed to explain those
residuals, it should be fitted on a training subset, frozen, and
tested elsewhere. Repeatedly explaining the same residuals with
new structural expressions would accumulate discrete model
flexibility even if no continuous parameter appears in the final
printed formula.
The most valuable next result would not be another decimal
place in the median. It would be a demonstrated map from
a galaxy’s baryonic surface-density profile and specified for-

11. A prospective test with explicit stopping rules
The proposed CR034 test should freeze 10/π, the stellar conventions, geometry, sample cuts, statistic, and uncertainty procedure before opening a genuinely untouched sample. A different
survey name is insufficient if many of its galaxies or rotation
measurements already occur in SPARC. Cross-matching objects and data provenance is part of protecting the holdout.
Candidate surveys named in the original draft include THINGS,
LITTLE THINGS, and PROBES; no claim is made here that
any particular subset is untouched.
The primary observable should be specified in advance. For
an outer-support test, use one defined outer estimator per galaxy
and retain failed or nonpositive residual cases under a declared
rule. The primary statistic can be the median log10 [X∞ /Xout ],
but a median alone can conceal broad or systematic failure.
Secondary diagnostics should include scatter, coverage, and
residual trends with surface brightness, gas fraction, mass, scale
length, outer acceleration, and radial extent. These diagnostics
test whether a common centre is hiding distinct populations.
Measurement uncertainty should propagate by drawing correlated galaxy-level nuisance variables and velocity uncertainties,
then recomputing the full estimator. Population uncertainty can
be estimated by resampling galaxies. Shared photometric or
stellar-population systematics require separate perturbations
rather than independent draws for each point. The final interval
should state which of these sources is included. The historical
±12% criterion can be retained as a declared centre tolerance,
but it must not be confused with a claim that individual halo
masses are predicted to twelve percent.
A minimal failure rule is that the frozen coordinate falls outside the prespecified population interval or exhibits a prespecified systematic residual that the claimed universality forbids. A
stronger radial-law claim must also predict the curve shape and
its scatter without fitting hidden galaxy-specific parameters. If
the holdout fails, selecting a new simple constant creates a new
hypothesis; it does not rescue the original prospective test. If it

A genuine prediction interval should combine intrinsic diversity with measurement uncertainty and uncertainty in any
population parameters learned from the training set. If the same
galaxies determine the scatter and assess its coverage, the apparent success is optimistic. A useful held-out report therefore
freezes the interval rule and counts how many new galaxies fall
inside it, while also publishing their distribution across mass
and surface brightness. Correct average coverage can conceal
systematic undercoverage in one physically important class.
The outer-radius selection can itself shift the centre. In the
explicit radial example above, observing a galaxy only to r = b
yields half the asymptotic support ratio, while reaching 9b
yields ninety percent. A population with different radial reach
can therefore have different outer medians even if every galaxy
obeys the same underlying law. This is a calculable selection
effect, not evidence of a changing fundamental constant. A
future test must either predict that effect from the radial law
or define a common physical radial domain before comparing
population centres.
The strongest use of a holdout is consequently two-stage.
First, predict the selected outer statistic with its observingwindow dependence. Second, predict the radial profile wherever
data are available, using the same frozen law. Passing the first
and failing the second would support a useful normalization
but reject the claim of a complete organization law. Passing
both with calibrated scatter would provide substantially more
evidence than another close median on the original sample.

(35)

A positive normalization requires 1 + q − p ≥ 0, with equality
describing an interval containing no additional halo density. If
the halo dominates a flat rotation curve, q = p and the density scales as r−2 in this local approximation. If the baryons
are already in their finite-mass exterior, p = 1, a constant support ratio gives no further halo mass growth. These relations
are simple but strong filters on any phenomenological radial
proposal.
Density recovery from measured curves is also an inverse
problem. Equation (21) differentiates data, amplifying shortscale noise. Smoothing can stabilize the derivative, but its scale
and functional restrictions can impose a core or cusp artificially.
A responsible analysis should forward-predict velocities from a
nonnegative density representation and compare that with any
direct inversion. Agreement between these routes is useful;
treating a noisy derivative as a unique local density is not.

15. Population precision versus individual prediction
The approximate 0.036 dex error of a population median should
not be used as the uncertainty of a new galaxy’s halo assignment.
To see the difference, assume for illustration that independent
future log mass ratios are normally distributed with centre zero
and standard deviation 0.38 dex. The central roughly 68%
interval for an individual ratio is then
10−0.38 < Mh,pred /Mh,obs < 100.38 ,

where j indexes radii, λ contains the frozen global physical law,
and νi denotes explicitly declared galaxy nuisance quantities. A
covariance-weighted residual uses the full within-galaxy matrix,
not one independent error for every appearance of the same
distance or inclination. If the observational input is a line-ofsight speed, the inclination projection belongs in the forward
model before comparison.
This formulation distinguishes two kinds of freedom. A
measured distance with an external uncertainty is a nuisance
input whose uncertainty should propagate. A new halo scale
chosen to minimize each galaxy’s residual is a model parameter.
Both may appear in an inference, but they cannot be counted
in the same way when claiming a parameter-free prediction.
Fixing a nuisance quantity at a convenient value can also make
a model appear more precise than the measurements allow.
The analysis should preserve the observed-velocity space
wherever possible because subtraction can create unstable ratios.

large even if both speeds are measured accurately. Taking a

An independent outer-mass observation would test more
than the median identity, but only if its inference is genuinely
independent. For example, a tracer-dynamics or lensing mass
estimate introduces its own anisotropy, projection, or geometry
assumptions. The right goal is not an assumption-free mass,
which is rarely available, but a comparison with sufficiently
different systematics and an explicit common physical model.
Agreement then supplies information that reexpressing the same
rotation speed in mass units cannot supply.
The eventual evidence package should therefore contain the
forward model, the complete nuisance policy, its training and
holdout split, residual plots in velocity and support space, and
calibrated prediction intervals. These objects allow another
investigator to distinguish a real radial prediction from a flexible
reconstruction. They also make a negative result useful: the
location and dependence of the failure can identify whether
the inventory normalization, radial organization, geometry, or
constituent interpretation needs revision.

Carrier radiation and ringdown dynamics
Chapter XI
Sean Brady
Originator and conceptual director
Research development with OpenAI ChatGPT and Codex
Unified expanded edition | 19 October 2026

Abstract. The carrier partition supplies three compact proposals: a radiated-energy ceiling of one eighth of an initial
source budget, a fundamental frequency coefficient 3/8, and a damping coefficient 4/45. Their arithmetic is exact, but their
interpretation as gravitational radiation requires a source-energy map, a physical unit chart and a causal field boundary condition.
This chapter proves the ceiling under explicit reservoir premises, derives an illustrative outgoing-flux identity, and formulates
the quasinormal-mode problem with a frequency-dependent surface response. It distinguishes the rational matches from the
Schwarzschild spectrum, includes the weak-field binary-radiation obligation, and explains why spin, excitation and mass
inference matter for observation. A worked finite pulse and independent arithmetic checks clarify which results are newly
established analytically and which remain source-record reports. The same boundary law must ultimately account for the
thermal behavior of Chapter VII and the perturbative response studied here.

1. Radiation as an interface between the source
and the exterior

must identify the clock, ruler and energy calibration inherited from the earlier source problem. It must also survive the
weak-field radiation tests that precede any strong-field ringdown
comparison.

The earlier chapters give the carrier sector a precise bookkeeping role. With radix R = 12, the closed container has R2 = 144
units, of which Θ = 18 are released and Mcount = 126 are retained. The original notation used M for the retained count and
also for a gravitating mass. Here the count receives a subscript; M f denotes the final compact-object mass. The distinction
prevents an exact integer identity from silently becoming a
dimensional energy statement.
The working interpretation is that a disturbance of the released sector can propagate away from a changing source. The
original chapter describes a merger as exposing carriers before
the common boundary closes. An isolated, perfectly spherical
formation would have no analogous time-dependent quadrupole
in the general-relativistic comparator. These are different statements. The first proposes a microscopic mechanism; the second
follows from the symmetry of a particular gravitational theory.
A useful carrier theory must specify which source variables excite its outgoing modes and explain the symmetry suppression
without relying on a verbal picture alone.
Several pieces of the required interface already exist elsewhere in the volume. Chapter I provides the source–field action
and its two receiving polarizations. Chapter IV retains nearfield, induction and radiative contributions in a finite-pulse
energy account. Chapter V supplies a causal boundary protocol with surface storage. Chapter VII asks how the same
boundary exchanges energy and information. None of these
ingredients should be discarded when constructing a radiation
model. Conversely, their existence does not establish that the
field has the tensor transformation law, source coupling and
asymptotic normalization of gravitational waves.
This chapter therefore has two levels. The first records the
original numerical proposals, including the 1/8 energy fraction
and the pair 3/8, 4/45. The second asks what action, boundary
response and measurement procedure would make those proposals physical predictions. A derivation at the second level

11. Stability, scale degeneracy and independent
information

Parameter uncertainty belongs to source mass, spin, orientation,
calibration and noise. Structural uncertainty belongs to the
choice of exterior action, boundary law and excitation model.
Shrinking the first budget to many significant figures does not
shrink the other two. The small rational residuals are interesting
precisely because they invite a clean calculation, but the claimed
precision must refer to the quantity actually constrained.

11.1 An energy test for a passive exterior
For the homogeneous comparator with V ≥ 0, its bulk energy
integral is nonnegative. Suppose the outer boundary carries
only outward flux and the inner boundary, including its storage
variables, is passive. Adding the surface energy to the bulk
identity yields a total energy that cannot increase after the drive
is removed. A finite-energy solution growing exponentially
in time would contradict this monotonicity unless it had zero
energy or violated one of the premises. This is a useful sufficient
stability screen for a proposed boundary model.
The screen must be applied to the complete energy, not only
to the exterior wave. Eliminating a driven surface oscillator can
make an effective boundary term look negative while its full
source account remains well behaved. Conversely, assuming a
passive reflection coefficient while omitting an active controller
can conceal a real energy supply. The sign and storage of the
counterterms inherited from the Original Write action therefore
require explicit attention.
Ordinary damped quasinormal eigenfunctions are not squareintegrable on the real tortoise line; their boundary behavior
under complex continuation is part of the resonance construction. The finite-energy monotonicity argument applies directly
to physical wave packets and admissible growing modes, not
to a naive norm of every damped resonance. It complements
a spectral calculation rather than replacing it. A trustworthy
computation reports both the pole search and a time-domain
response to a finite, paid pulse.

Finally, total energy and detector observability are different
questions. A signal may have finite energy but negligible projection in a particular instrument, or significant projection in a
narrow band while much energy lies elsewhere. To turn a carrier budget into a catalog prediction, the model needs the angular
pattern, spectrum, source orientation and detector response as

from a physical source, not nuisance details that can be omitted
because the final energy ceiling is dimensionless.
A practical benefit of these solved comparators is that each
failure can be localized. An incorrect flux normalization
changes the relation between amplitude and energy without
moving the oscillator poles. A changed damping bath changes
absorption and pole widths even when the restoring frequency
is unchanged. A different observation window changes template overlap without changing the underlying field equation.
Keeping these operations distinct prevents an improved fit at
one interface from being presented as a derivation at another.
The source theory must eventually select all three: the dynamics
that creates a signal, the energy account that pays for it, and
the measurement channel that makes it visible. The checks
supplied here deliberately test those interfaces separately. Their
agreement is a consistency requirement on the illustrative mathematics; it is not additional independent evidence for the carrier
ontology. That distinction leaves a clear path for replacing each
comparator by the native calculation when the corresponding
source and boundary operands become available.

Chapter XII

Abstract. The closing chapter brings together two different structures: a line-of-sight accumulation law with saturation 1/π,
and a matter-inventory assignment with the same numerical value. Their equality is exact within the declared count rules, but a
cosmological future requires a time-evolution law and a calibrated observable. We distinguish a distance-fit coefficient from
3/2
the fractional expansion rate, derive the conditions under which the original ΩΛ expression is meaningful, and formulate
finite-redshift tests. The completed-boundary or Home continuation is then developed as an explicit conditional ledger, with
conservation, radius-floor and information-channel requirements. A worked receipt sequence demonstrates growth while
emitting, and a differential distance test exposes the assumptions hidden in a simple rate rescaling. The resulting closure program
connects the thermal boundary, radiation response and cosmological inventory without treating their common numerical factors
as a substitute for dynamics. No transition mechanism or future cosmological solution is claimed to have been established by
count identities alone.

1. The two arcs that meet at the end of the volume

2. The road law and what it actually proves

Volume I begins with a floor and a source-induced lift. The
floor supplies a reference level; the lift describes an accumulation attributed to a particular source. Chapters III–VII follow
the source coordinate toward a completed boundary and ask
how clocks, records, fields and thermal exchange behave there.
Chapters VIII–X use the floor in a proposed cosmic inventory and in the organization of many-source systems. Chapter
XI asks whether the released carrier account can become an
independently testable radiation law.
The original ending joins these arcs in two ways. First, it
identifies the limiting line-of-sight road accumulation with the
matter fraction. Second, it proposes that a completed Home can
supply a new floor through a change of informational indexing.
Both are substantial ideas. Neither should be weakened by
asking a numerical identity to establish a causal process that
has not yet been specified.
This chapter therefore keeps the original proposals while
separating four levels of statement. An identity follows from
the chosen counts. A conditional theorem follows after its physical premises are declared. An adapter imports a conventional
geometry or evolution law. A conjecture identifies a possible
continuation whose mechanism remains to be found. The end
of the volume is strongest when these levels remain visible,
because they show exactly which result a future calculation
would add.
The word “fate” also requires care. The future of a cosmological solution is a statement about evolution in proper time.
The saturation of an integral along the present past light cone is
a statement about progressively more distant emission events.
A change of radial distance convention is yet another operation. The three can be related by a theory, but they cannot be
interchanged by notation.
